title: 1995 AHSME Problem 7
statement: The radius of Earth at the equator is approximately \(4000\) miles. Suppose a jet flies once around Earth at a speed of \(500\) miles per hour relative to Earth. If the flight path is a negligible height above the equator, then, among the following choices, the best estimate of the number of hours of flight is

solutions.text: The equator is approximately \(2\pi(4000)=8000\pi\) miles long. The flight time is \(\frac{8000\pi}{500}=16\pi\approx50\) hours. Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: Approximate the equator’s length with \(2\pi r\)
Divide the trip distance by \(500\) and use a simple estimate for \(\pi\)
